heading: Weak-to-strong generalization extends to vision
summary: Several independent groups reproduce weak-to-strong generalization in vision, including image classification and video quality assessment. Gains depend on the task, training method and evaluation conditions, with failures in some settings.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: R0 for modified-MNIST parity gains at nst=1000 and 1500; C at nst=500; limits_scope for small positive gains at nst=2000 and 2500 (arXiv:2510.24812#R16, arXiv:2510.24812#R18, arXiv:2510.24812#R14, arXiv:2510.24812#R20, arXiv:2510.24812#R22). <1B: ? for a size-specific level; counts: V6.studies_by_size.<1B = 3 does not identify successful student settings. Vision encoders with unstated parameter counts: R2 for ImageNet linear probes (arXiv:2606.01292#r8, arXiv:2606.01292#r9, arXiv:2606.01292#r10). 1-10B: R2 for out-of-distribution video quality assessment, with in-domain challenges (arXiv:2505.03631#R2, arXiv:2505.03631#R1). 10-100B: ?; counts: V6.studies_by_size.10-100B = 1, but V6.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size has no 10-100B entry. >100B: ?; absent from V6.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: R2 remains appropriate for the vision effect under tested conditions. AlexNet-supervised linear probes on pretrained DINO vision encoders recover the weak-to-ceiling gap on an ImageNet subset, with qualitative, figure-based evidence (arXiv:2606.01292#r8, arXiv:2606.01292#r9, arXiv:2606.01292#r10). Counts: V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0 records no shared authors among tested studies; this does not establish author independence for every linked source. Challenges must be condition-specific: negative ImageNet-C results warrant challenges, while small positive corruption results remain limits_scope (arXiv:2510.21332#r03, arXiv:2510.21332#r07). Video students exceed teachers out of distribution but comparable or equal in-domain outcomes warrant challenges (arXiv:2505.03631#R2, arXiv:2505.03631#R1, arXiv:2505.03631#R13). Modified-MNIST outcomes likewise depend on pseudo-label set size (arXiv:2510.24812#R14, arXiv:2510.24812#R16, arXiv:2510.24812#R20). Counts: V6.verdicts.supports.studies = 18, V6.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 9 and V6.verdicts.challenges.studies = 5 are supplied pre-revision totals, not totals recomputed after checker corrections.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent failed replication under matched AlexNet-to-DINO ImageNet conditions would move that setting toward C. Matched student-supervisor and ground-truth-trained comparisons would clarify PGR across modalities, scales and distribution shifts. Video quality assessment already includes a ground-truth-trained comparison for its 27k condition, so the remaining question is broader coverage rather than universal absence of a ceiling. Explicit student parameter counts and weak-label training tests above 10B would clarify the scale-specific levels. Tests outside vision would establish whether the effect extends further.

source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Collin Burns; Pavel Izmailov; J. Kirchner; Bowen Baker; Leo Gao; Leopold Aschenbrenner; Yining Chen; Adrien Ecoffet; Manas R. Joglekar; Jan Leike; I. Sutskever; Jeff Wu

original_result.setup: They trained linear probes on DINO vision encoders using AlexNet-generated labels for ImageNet classification.
original_result.result: DINO ResNet50 reached 60.7% accuracy and DINO ViT-B/8 reached 64.2%, exceeding AlexNet’s 56.6%. They recovered 57.8% and 41.5% of the gap to ground-truth supervision, respectively.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: S+S+C students outperformed zero-shot labellers on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+.
Vision students achieved positive gap recovery, with further improvements from co-supervised learning.
ResNet-50 students outperformed all three CNN supervisors on CIFAR-10.
SDXL trained on SD v2 images outperformed its supervisor across all evaluated metrics.
CNN and ViT students achieved positive gap recovery using teacher labels alone.
Qwen2-VL 7B outscored its 2B supervisor on Arena-Hard.
Students improved average accuracy over teachers across four vision datasets with matched spurious correlations.
Vision linear probes recovered performance gaps across tested UTKFace teachers and noise levels.
Weakly supervised CNNs outperformed MLP supervisors at two modified MNIST training sizes.
CPL enabled CLIP students to outperform vision supervisors across most tested settings.
DINO students surpassed AlexNet supervision in loss and accuracy on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
TransMiter targets surpassed fine-tuned weak supervisors across reported classification and detection settings.
Nuclei segmentation students surpassed SAM-C on AJI+, PQ, and coverage.
Naive vision transfer achieved positive gap recovery under saturation and brightness corruptions.
Video quality students outperformed teachers across all evaluated out-of-distribution aggregates.
Autoregressive image students usually surpassed supervisors in subject fidelity.
The caption reports gap recovery for five vision students trained with AlexNet supervision.
DINO ResNet50 surpassed its AlexNet supervisor on ImageNet.
RefCOCOg gains were small, with nearly unchanged validation oIoU.
Vision gap recovery weakened when supervisors lagged far behind students.
Modified MNIST gains vanished or remained small at other training sizes.
Standard CLIP fine-tuning usually failed, while CPL gains remained small on Quickdraw and Real.
TransMiter gains were small with the strongest supervisor and mostly reflected zero-shot ability under shifts.
Nuclei segmentation gains were small, with no meaningful improvement in marker purity.
Naive vision gap recovery was negative or negligible under most evaluated ImageNet-C corruptions.
Naive video quality fine-tuning showed no clear in-domain improvement over teachers.
Image generation gains weakened for prompt fidelity and failed for diffusion students.
Naive pseudo-mask training mostly failed to surpass the zero-shot segmentation supervisor.
Compact medical-imaging students showed no meaningful AUC gain over VLM labelers.
Naive distillation into ViT-L/14 underperformed its fine-tuned ViT-B/16 supervisor.
LlamaGen underperformed its FLUX supervisor across all three evaluated image generation metrics.
OPD visual tool-use students averaged below their Qwen2.5-VL supervisor across checkpoints.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Non-vision modalities outside language (audio, speech, tabular, time series, graphs, control/RL). Every tested study in the pack is image, video or vision-language.
untested.basis: Pack study list and 'untested parts of V6' lines (2402.15505: modalities other than image classification; 2509.24005 and 2510.21332: other modalities; 2501.19105 and 2606.01292: other modalities untested). No counts key records modality.

untested.what: Vision or vision-language weak-label-trained students above 10B. Tested video-quality students include InternVL3-8B and a LLaVA-based student with 8075.24M total parameters, so the previous 7B upper bound was incorrect.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has '10-100B': 1 and no '>100B' key; versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size has neither bucket. The checker for arXiv:2505.03631 identifies InternVL3-8B in Table 9 and the main student's 8075.24M parameters in Table 7 (student comparisons: arXiv:2505.03631#R9 and arXiv:2505.03631#R10), with no student above 10B reported. Wan-Fun-14B in arXiv:2609.05968#r16 is a frozen host receiving sampling-time guidance, not a weak-label-trained student.

untested.what: True-label strong-ceiling comparisons for normalized PGR in multiplex microscopy segmentation and image generation; complete image-conditioned weak-supervisor and true-label-ceiling comparisons for VLM alignment.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation does not distinguish true-label ceilings or PGR reporting. Study-specific gaps: arXiv:2512.11722#R1 and arXiv:2512.11722#R2 have no true-label ceiling or PGR; arXiv:2403.06952#r1 and arXiv:2503.10125#R1 likewise lack true-label ceilings and PGR. For VLM alignment, arXiv:2410.18640#r29 is an Arena-Hard comparison without an established image-conditioned evaluation; image-question rows arXiv:2410.18640#r30 and arXiv:2410.18640#r31 lack weak-supervisor scores, and the study reports no true-label ceiling.

wording_issues.issue: V1 defines the effect as PGR > 0 relative to a true-label-trained strong ceiling, while V6 includes raw-metric comparisons without that ceiling, such as AJI+/PQ in 2512.11722. This does not apply uniformly: 2505.03631 Table 1 includes a ground-truth-trained strong student, making aggregate PGR calculable, though not author-reported; no 200k ground-truth-trained counterpart is provided. For 2508.08604's PromptSRC ViT-B/16→ViT-L/14 aggregate, source FT is 81.74%, target zero-shot 72.54%, target FT 85.17%, and TransMiter 82.51%. In 2511.18396, checker-computed PGR fractions are 0.391–0.899 for Table 1 excluding Real, 0.909–0.965 for the Table 5 backbone sweep, and 1.292 for Table 1 Real, whose denominator is only 0.24 percentage points. These are not author-reported PGR values.

The statement doesn't say whether naive weak-label training is meant. In 2310.13479, ZSBootstrap underperforms the S+S labeller on mIoU and on oIoU except RefCOCO val and testA; S+S+C gives substantially larger improvements on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+. In 2511.18396, DomainNet Clipart CE+LP accuracy is 66.97% versus weak 67.15%, a numerical reversal without a significance or negligibility assessment; CPL reaches 73.10% against a 74.27% strong ceiling. In 2508.08604, classification PromptKD from ViT-B/16 into ViT-L/14 scores 78.75% versus source FT 81.74%. Added methods include S+S+C, CPL, TransMiter and co-supervision; their results should be distinguished from naive training.

'Vision' covers classification, regression, segmentation, generation, video quality and visual tool use, with outcomes depending on task, metric and method. In 2505.03631, naive LLaVA-OneVision-Chat-7B students trained on 27k videos approximately match teachers in-domain and exceed them OOD; some naive 200k students also gain slightly in-domain. The enhanced LLaVA method improves in-domain SRCC from 0.849 to 0.865 and OOD SRCC from 0.591 to 0.745. In 2609.08798's agentic visual tool use, the five-checkpoint aggregate is reversed relative to the teacher: OPD 65.57 versus teacher 67.74, despite exceeding the initial student's 54.83.

No non-vision modality is tested. A vision-language model's architecture alone does not establish an effect outside language. In 2410.18640, Qwen2-VL 2B→7B on Arena-Hard scores 5.80 versus weak DPO 1.50, supporting V1, but Table 10 does not establish an image-conditioned student–supervisor comparison: V6 is cannot_determine. Its image-question benchmark, MMHal-Bench, lacks weak-supervisor scores in r30–r31.

Some pairs are not clearly weak-supervises-strong. In 2505.03631 the Q-Align teacher (8.2B) is about the student's size (R9, R10). In 173d42ed a BiomedCLIP labeller supervises 8M-parameter DenseNet-121 students. In 2512.11722 the student sees 8 channels while the teacher sees 2. In 2503.10125 the verdict calls diffusion-to-diffusion not clearly weak-to-strong.

In some settings the strong model already beats the supervisor before any weak-label training, so 'beats the supervisor' says little. SELMA: SDXL base 73.3 vs SD v2 70.3 on DSG and 83.5 vs 79.2 on TIFA; after training PickScore is 21.5, below base 21.6. TransMiter novel classes: zero-shot 80.85 vs supervisor 75.35 (verdict).

method_sensitivity.what: With an AlexNet supervisor and DINO ResNet50 student, naive PGR is positive for Saturate (20.94 ± 1.09) and Brightness (16.93 ± 0.74), but negative for Zoom blur (−5.36 ± 0.42) and JPEG (−4.42 ± 0.36). The negative-corruption subgroup reverses the vision effect and warrants challenges; positive-corruption conditions remain separate.

DomainNet Clipart accuracy (%): weak 67.15; CE+LP 66.97 and CE+TP 62.02 are below weak (challenges), while CPL reaches 73.10 against a strong ceiling of 74.27. No significance or equivalence assessment is reported for CE+LP. ViT-B/16→ViT-L/14 base-to-base, PromptSRC: PromptKD 78.75, TransMiter 82.51, source FT 81.74, target zero-shot 72.54, target FT 85.17; TransMiter's gain over source FT is 0.77 percentage points. CIFAR-100 accuracy (%): KD 77.92 versus AdaptConf 78.48 (ShuffleNet-V1 → ResNet32×4); KD is the method-gain comparator, while itself showing the V6 effect. Co-supervision with denoising: more than 15% PGR over vanilla on ImageNet.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data budget (pseudo-label set size, gold-label budget)
method_sensitivity.what: Modified MNIST test accuracy (%): CNN student below MLP at nst=500 (84.62 vs 86.06; challenges), above at nst=1000/1500 (88.34 vs 85.93; 88.46 vs 86.42), with small positive mean gains at 2000/2500 (limits_scope); SDs do not establish significance. PCAM, gold/weak mixtures: student AUC at ng=10/100/500 is 0.846/0.851/0.844 versus approximate teacher ceiling 0.84 (partial V6; PGR unreported). Against gold-only training, weak augmentation helps at ng=10 (0.846 vs 0.579 ± 0.094), but falls below at ng=100 (0.851 vs 0.868 ± 0.003), ng=500 (0.844 vs 0.922), ng=1,000 (0.857 vs 0.936) and ng=5,000 (0.874 vs 0.970). 2502.05075: the outcome depends on n and N (figure-only).

Subject-driven generation: Lumina-mGPT beats SDXL on CLIP-I (0.8074 vs 0.8002) but not on CLIP-T (0.3118 vs 0.3225). Nuclei segmentation: M3-RCNN beats SAM-C on AJI+ (77.3% vs 76.0%) and PQ, but marker purity is numerically below the teacher on S4 (99.01% vs 99.02%; reversed); statistical significance is not established. SELMA: above SDXL base on DSG and HPS, below it on PickScore (21.5 vs 21.6).

method_sensitivity.factor: In-domain vs OOD / base vs novel evaluation
method_sensitivity.what: Naive video-quality training with FAST-VQA supervision shows no demonstrated gain in-domain (student SRCC 0.836 vs teacher 0.838; challenges for this absent-effect condition), but exceeds the teacher OOD (0.543 vs 0.486). This does not classify the separate small positive in-domain gains from some 200k conditions as absent. TransMiter: base accuracy 85.27 vs source 84.19 (PGR-like fraction ≈0.36). Novel accuracy is 81.07 vs 75.35, largely explained by the zero-shot target (80.85, verdict).

With AlexNet supervision, PGR decreases monotonically as the capability gap widens (2402.15505, figure-only): V3 dependence is observed, while V6 recovery is partial under large gaps. TransMiter, ViT-B/16→ViT-L/14 accuracy (%): CoOp source FT 79.92, target zero-shot 72.54, target FT 84.57, TransMiter 82.05; PromptSRC source FT 81.74, target zero-shot 72.54, target FT 85.17, TransMiter 82.51 (gain over source FT 0.77 percentage points). UTKFace: teachers with lower feature-subspace overlap give better relative PGR, and ResNet34 does relatively worse. ColoredMNIST representation trends establish V3 dependence, but absolute PGR is unavailable, so V6 is cannot_determine for r12. LlamaGen falls below FLUX on all three subject-generation metrics.

More injected noise gives higher PGR: on UTKFace with a ResNet50 teacher, PGR is positive across noise levels (figure-axis range about 0.55–0.8, not individual measurements) and rises with noise. On ColoredMNIST, more label-flip noise gives higher PGR (trend only, figure-only), establishing V3 dependence. The ColoredMNIST trend does not establish PGR above zero; V6 is cannot_determine for r13.

SELMA: SDXL trained on SD v2-generated data reaches HPS 28.8, while SDXL trained on its own generated images reaches 29.9 (verdict on r5). The study's method-sensitivity line reports the reverse ordering on DSG.
